original_question: For a germ tangent to the identity in C^n, describe the stable set using invariants attached to characteristic directions (including directors and indices), and determine what additional invariants are needed to capture the full structure of the stable set.
target_in_paper: §3.5, Open Problem OP14: "Describe, using characteristic directions, directors, indices and possibly other invariants, the stable set of a germ tangent to the identity in C^n."
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper's target very closely: it is about holomorphic germs tangent to the identity in C^n, asks for a description of the stable set, singles out characteristic directions together with directors and indices as the main invariants, and correctly reflects the paper's point that these may not suffice and that further invariants may be needed.
missing_details: The paper works with a holomorphic local dynamical system f in End(C^n,0), i.e. a germ of a holomorphic self-map fixing 0; this should be stated explicitly.

The stable set should be defined: for a representative f:U→C^n, K_f = ⋂_{k≥0} f^{-k}(U), equivalently the set of points in U whose forward orbit is well-defined; the problem concerns the germ at 0 of K_f.
"Tangent to the identity" should be made explicit as f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+P_{ν+1}(z)+⋯ with ν≥2 and P_ν a nonzero homogeneous polynomial map of degree ν (equivalently d f_0 = Id); ν is the multiplicity.
A characteristic direction should be defined: [v] in P^{n-1}(C) with v≠0 and P_ν(v)=λv for some λ in C; the paper also distinguishes degenerate (λ=0) and non-degenerate (λ≠0) directions.

The ambient projective space P^{n-1}(C) and the fact that directors/indices are attached to characteristic directions should be stated; the paper notes that directors and indices are not literally the same numbers, though they are strongly related.
The nearby context says the issue is to describe the stable set in a full neighborhood of the origin, not merely the one-dimensional dynamics on parabolic curves/Fatou flowers.

The paper emphasizes that K_f can be strictly larger than the set of points whose orbits converge to 0 tangentially to some characteristic direction, so a stand-alone formulation should leave room for such non-tangential or otherwise anomalous stable behavior.
refined_question: Let f ∈ End(C^n,0) be a holomorphic germ tangent to the identity, so that f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+P_{ν+1}(z)+⋯ with ν≥2 and P_ν a nonzero homogeneous polynomial map of degree ν. For a representative f:U→C^n, let K_f=⋂_{k≥0} f^{-k}(U) be its stable set, and for each characteristic direction [v]∈P^{n-1}(C) of f (i.e. P_ν(v)=λv for some λ∈C), consider the associated directors/indices. Describe the germ at 0 of K_f, not just the subset of points whose orbits converge to 0 tangentially to a characteristic direction, in terms of the characteristic directions and their directors/indices, and determine what further invariants, if any, are needed to account for the whole stable set.
justification: The draft clearly targets §3.5 rather than the paper's earlier general questions: it is essentially a paraphrase of OP14. To make it stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import the paper's definitions of stable set from Definition 2 in the introduction, and of tangent-to-the-identity germs and characteristic directions from §3.4. The immediate context of OP14 explains why the problem is sharper than merely describing attracting Fatou flowers: Theorems 14 and 15 only give one-dimensional pieces of the dynamics, Hakim's criterion shows how directors control attracting flowers near non-degenerate directions, and the paragraph before OP14 states that the stable set may also contain points not converging tangentially to any direction and even nearby periodic orbits, which is why the paper explicitly allows "possibly other invariants."
